newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU changes Spain, Portugal cereal, oilseed area aid.
newsitem.headline: EU changes Spain, Portugal cereal, oilseed area aid.

text.p: European Union grain officials have approved changes to Spanish and Portuguese area aid schemes for cereals, oilseeds and protein crops, a member state official said on Monday.
Spain's overall base area eligible for EU subsidies remains unchanged at 9.22 million hectares despite adjustments to the irrigated and dry-land areas.
The Spanish so-called regado area -- mainly irrigated land -- was increased to 1.37 million hectares, from 1.23 million ha.
But regional so-called secana, or dry-land, base areas have been trimmed and combined into a single national base area.

In a separate move, the officials approved changes to Spanish regional reference yields. The changes do not alter the overall historic yield upon which EU subsidy payments are based, the official stressed.
The Spanish regado yield was cut to 4.6 tonnes per hectare, from 5.6 tonnes while the secano yield was raised to 2.2 tonnes per hectare, from 2.1 tonnes.
"The regado yield was miscalculated when Spain joined the EU (in 1986)," the official said, noting a 10-year tax relief period for this kind of production.
For Portugal, EU officials agreed to raise the regado area by 40,000 hectares to 275,000 ha, while cutting the secano area by 13,200 ha to 755,100 ha.
Separately, they agreed to reduce regional reference yields by 10 to 15 percent while keeping the overall historic yield unchanged as a result of adjustments to the regional plans.
The changes to the Spanish and Portuguese arable area schemes will take effect after publication in the EU Official Journal.
